title: Hospitality
summary: Hospitality was a deeply important social duty in the ancient world, especially for travelers, strangers, and guests.
background: Welcoming someone into a home often involved honor, protection, provision, washing, food, and fellowship. Scripture uses hospitality to reveal faith, love, and obedience.
teachingHelp: When teaching hospitality, connect the custom to covenant kindness, mercy to strangers, and the Gospel-shaped welcome of God.
sources: James M. Freeman, Hand-book of Bible Manners and Customs (1874 / early public-domain editions).
Alfred Edersheim, Sketches of Jewish Social Life in the Days of Christ (1876).
International Standard Bible Encyclopedia, original 1915 edition.
